arguments.code:
SurveyCrawler comment: 'I am a seabed survey crawler. I know the position I am at, the direction I am facing, the sonar I sense the ground with and the run I am processing commands in.

I process a sequence of commands where $a advances, $t retreats, $h turns me clockwise, $g turns me counter clockwise, a digit repeats the last of those commands its value plus two times, and $( and $) delimit a guarded run, whose movements I undo when something goes wrong.

For example: (SurveyCrawler at: 1@2 facing: #Up) process: ''aa(ht3)''.'.

CrawlerFacing comment: 'I am the direction a survey crawler is facing. I know the displacement it makes when it advances and the facings it gets when it turns clockwise or counter clockwise.

My subclasses are the four directions of the seabed grid, and each one is created by name with CrawlerFacing facing: #Up.'.

CrawlerSonar comment: 'I am the sonar of a survey crawler. I know the ground of the positions of the seabed that are not firm sand, and I answer the ground a crawler will end up on when it moves to a position.

For example: CrawlerSonar detecting: { 1@3 -> BoulderGround new }'.

SeabedGround comment: 'I am the ground of a position of the seabed. I know the displacement a crawler really makes when it tries to move by a displacement onto me, and whether it can turn while standing on me.'.

FirmSandGround comment: 'I am firm sand, the ground a survey crawler moves and turns on as expected.'.

BoulderGround comment: 'I am a boulder. A survey crawler can neither move onto me nor turn while standing on me, so I signal an error whenever it tries.'.

SiltGround comment: 'I am silt. A survey crawler that moves onto me slides an unpredictable number of cells, never more than my maximum slide distance, in the direction it was going. Turning on me is as safe as turning on firm sand.

I know the generator that decides how far a crawler slides, which lets a deterministic one be used while testing.'.

CrawlerRun comment: 'I am the run a survey crawler is processing its commands in. I know how a crawler is affected by silt, whether a guarded run can be started or finished, whether the sequence of commands ended when it should have, and I keep the actions that undo what the crawler did.'.

CrawlerNormalRun comment: 'I am an unguarded run. A crawler slides on silt while running me, nothing it does has to be undone, and a guarded run can be started but not finished within me.'.

CrawlerGuardedRun comment: 'I am a guarded run, the one a survey crawler processes the commands between $( and $) in. I know the actions that undo every movement and every turn the crawler made since I started, so it can return to where it was when anything goes wrong.

Movement on silt is unpredictable, so I do not allow it, and neither do I allow another guarded run to be started within me.'.

CrawlerCommand comment: 'I am one of the commands a survey crawler processes. I know how to execute myself on a crawler, knowing the command executed before me, and I answer the command the crawler has to remember as the last one executed.

My class knows which command each character of a sequence of commands means.'.

CrawlerRepeatableCommand comment: 'I am a command that can be repeated by the digit written after me.'.

CrawlerAdvanceCommand comment: 'I am the command $a, which makes a survey crawler advance.'.
CrawlerRetreatCommand comment: 'I am the command $t, which makes a survey crawler retreat.'.
CrawlerTurnClockwiseCommand comment: 'I am the command $h, which makes a survey crawler turn clockwise.'.
CrawlerTurnCounterClockwiseCommand comment: 'I am the command $g, which makes a survey crawler turn counter clockwise.'.
CrawlerRepetitionCommand comment: 'I am a digit written after a repeatable command. I know how many more times that command has to be executed, which is my digit value plus two.'.
CrawlerNoCommand comment: 'I am the command a survey crawler remembers when there is no previous command to repeat, either because it has not executed any yet or because the last one it executed can not be repeated. Trying to repeat me is an invalid command.'.
CrawlerStartGuardedRunCommand comment: 'I am the command $(, which makes a survey crawler start a guarded run.'.
CrawlerEndGuardedRunCommand comment: 'I am the command $), which makes a survey crawler finish the guarded run it is processing.'.
FixedSlideDistanceGenerator comment: 'I generate always the same slide distance, so that sliding on silt can be tested without depending on chance.'.
SurveyCrawlerTest comment: 'I test a seabed survey crawler.'.

slideDisplacementFor: aDisplacement

	^aDisplacement * self slideDistance

slideDisplacementFor: aDisplacement on: aSiltGround

	^aSiltGround slideDisplacementFor: aDisplacement

processCommandsIn: aCommandStream

	| lastCommand |
	
	lastCommand := CrawlerNoCommand new.
	[ aCommandStream atEnd ] whileFalse: [
		lastCommand := (CrawlerCommand for: aCommandStream next) 
			executeAfter: lastCommand 
			on: self ].
	run assertIsFinished

abortRun

	| interruptedRun |
	
	"The interrupted run is replaced before undoing it so that undoing does not register new undo actions"
	interruptedRun := run.
	self continueWith: CrawlerNormalRun new.
	interruptedRun undoAll
